ruling.recommended_action: Hold the case for human review: obtain the driver's full GPS coverage for the uncovered final stretch (last 4 min before 14:33:55) before any refund is computed; no refund now.
ruling.reasoning:
The rider complains the driver took a different way and that the meter ran to 10.10 km against an estimate of 7.7 km, asking for the extra distance to be refunded; the fare record confirms 10.10 km billed at $1.4099/km with no surge [F7][F6][RD-2].

The record does not cover the whole trip: the GPS trace's last sample is 4 min 0 s before the 14:33:55 drop-off, and what happened outside the covered stretch is not on record [F1]. The measured deviation within the covered stretch is only +0.3 km (8.0 km vs 7.7 km), which is inside the 1 km tolerance [F2][RD-1], whereas the off-route segment 14:27–14:29 alone adds 1.23 km [F4]. Because part of the trip cannot be measured, an outcome-relevant distance (and any exempt km) cannot be settled, and a missing or broken GPS track must not be read for or against either side [F1][TH-4].

The only rider message that could bear on the disputed segment is Chat #3 at 14:29, which asks to go via Canning Lane and be dropped at the other side of Clarke Quay [F10]; that came during/after the off-route segment that began at 14:27 [F4], so I cannot complete a segment finding on prior consent, and the driver's post-trip statement that the GPS rerouted him is a claim, not consent [F12][RD-5]. Eu Tong Sen Street and Kampong Bahru Road both show fast speed bands and no traffic incident is recorded, so no traffic reason excuses the deviation [F13][F14][F15][RD-4]; the weather is fine [F16]. No consent scope or stop under RD-3 can be fixed on this record [F10][RD-3].

The chat, the driver's statement and the complaint contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — the messages are a pickup arrangement and a routing request [F8][F9][F10][F12] — so the safety screen is clear [SAFE-1].

Both advocates request no_action, but on this record a refund cannot be quantified and the outcome cannot be settled, so the case goes to a person [TH-4]. Profile facts do not decide the case: the rider has no upheld disputes and the driver has one upheld dispute of another type [F17][F18][RD-6].
